8"""GCU400-specific ``_foreach_log2`` (out-of-place): delegates to the shared unary executor. 

9 

10Older versions used a standalone int64-metadata single-launch kernel to bypass the shared 

11executor's grid.y hardware cap, but the wrapper rebuilt metadata on the host every call (3xNT 

12CPU tensor-scalar writes plus one pageable H2D, measured ~136us) and then went through an 

13uncached Triton dispatch (~15us): in official bench kernel mode every 256^2/512^2/1024^2 x 16 

14tier ran ~105-213us with weak shape correlation (2026-11-16 local baseline 0.64-0.92x). The 

15lean single-launch route in ``_foreach_unary.py`` here (host ~8us for same-dtype contiguous 

16float lists, ``_device_meta`` memoized by pointer list plus launch replay, see the 2026-11-16 

1724-variant campaign) already scales BLOCK by powers of two to bring grid.y under 255, and the 

18log2 row fn uses the mathematically equivalent ``tl.log(x)*log2(e)`` (log costs 8-17% less per 

19call, same precedent as ``_foreach_log2_``), so out-of-place also delegates to that executor. 

20 

21Non-float, non-contiguous, mixed dtype/device and complex inputs fall back to ``apply_unary``'s 

22shared grouped path; dtype promotion (integer/bool output float32) and error semantics are unchanged. 

23""" 

24 

25import logging 

26 

27from ._foreach_unary import apply_unary 

28 

29logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

30 

31 

32def _foreach_log2(self): 

33 logger.debug("GEMS_GCU400 FOREACH_LOG2") 

34 return apply_unary("log2", self, inplace=False)
